## Overview

Fix Python DeepSeek V4.1 rendering when tool results reorder image placeholders or thinking mode drops historical developer content. Carry source image indices through the native encoder and apply the resulting order to both image data and UUIDs.

This follows the source-order approach of #56366, which fixed the Rust frontend only.

## Claims

- Out-of-order tool results keep their own images after sorting into tool-call order.
- Images belonging to dropped developer content no longer reach multimodal prompt expansion without a placeholder.

## Validation

Two regression cases, each exercised through sync and async rendering; the existing V4/V4.1 tokenizer suites are also included.

| CPU tests | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Main implementation + regression tests | 4 failed, 75 passed |
| Patched implementation | 79 passed |

Run in a CPU-only container against the source checkout, with model/processor metadata stubbed and real message parsing, image tracking and native encoding:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=/work/checks/tests/tokenizers_ -o addopts= \
  /work/checks/tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py \
  /work/checks/tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py -v
```

Full pre-commit checks passed on all five changed files, including mypy and test CI tethering.

**GPU validation passed** on the real DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash checkpoint (`DeepseekV41ForCausalLM`), using 8x H20-3e, TP=8, eager execution and temperature=0. The GPU runtime was vLLM 0.31.0 / PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 with this PR's four production files mounted unchanged; their SHA-256 hashes were verified against commit `f5622b6`.

The same loaded model compared the original media handling (the base renderer without an image-order accumulator) and the patched V4.1 renderer:

| Full-model case | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Ordered tool results, baseline | `A=red, B=blue` |
| Reversed tool results, baseline | `A=blue, B=red` (wrong image assignment) |
| Reversed tool results, patched | `A=red, B=blue`; output token IDs match the ordered baseline |
| Dropped historical developer image, baseline | `AssertionError: Failed to apply prompt replacement for mm_items['image'][0]` |
| Dropped historical developer image, patched | Successful generation, final answer `OK` |

The validation script completed successfully with exit code 0. This verifies correctness, not performance.

## Details

The encoder already decides which content survives and in what order it renders. Image indices now follow those same merge/sort/drop operations; the renderer does not duplicate those policies or scan text for image markers. The V4.1 renderer applies the order to media and UUIDs together. Existing prompt fixtures and rendering parity checks retain the encoded text.

Duplicate checks covered open PRs, the related Rust PR's changed files and discussion, and V4.1 frontend searches. #56366 changes Rust files only; #60522 only moves Python imports and does not fix this behavior. No matching Python fix was found.

`_build_prompt` unpacks `rendered` as `(prompt_raw, image_order)`, and `render_messages_async` now passes `_apply_chat_template_async(...)` directly into `_build_prompt`. Since this PR only updates `_apply_chat_template` to return a tuple, you should ensure `_apply_chat_template_async` also returns the same tuple shape; otherwise async rendering will fail at runtime with an unpacking/type error (and V4.1 may silently skip image reordering in async paths). A concrete fix is to override `_apply_chat_template_async` in these renderers to delegate to the (tuple-returning) `_apply_chat_template` via an executor/`make_async`, so both sync and async share the same contract.

A concrete fix is to override `_apply_chat_template_async` in these renderers to delegate to the (tuple-returning) `_apply_chat_template` via an executor/`make_async`, so both sync and async share the same contract.

`parse_dec_only_prompt` expects a string prompt, but `prompt_raw` comes from `tokenizer.apply_chat_template(...)`, which can also return token IDs (e.g., when `tokenize=True`). With the new tuple-based plumbing, passing a tokenized result would break here. If `render_messages(*)` is intended to always operate on raw prompts, consider enforcing `tokenize=False` at the renderer boundary (e.g., override/strip the kwarg) or add a clear error when `prompt_raw` is not `str` to avoid hard-to-debug failures.

`DeepseekV4Renderer.__init__` already initializes the async wrapper with:

```python
self._apply_chat_template_async = make_async(
    self._apply_chat_template, executor=self._executor
)
```

This binds the overridden method on `DeepseekV41Renderer` as well, so both sync and async paths return `(prompt_raw, image_order)`. A separate async override should therefore not be necessary.

[Constructor and renderer implementation at the current PR head](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9a4453bf5e51db95dc46319db5a6080e6328ee22/vllm/renderers/deepseek_v4.py).

This is the same async-contract concern as the earlier comment; the existing constructor already wraps `self._apply_chat_template` with `make_async`, including the V4.1 override. The awaited result is therefore the same `(prompt_raw, image_order)` tuple consumed by `_build_prompt`.

I've added the constructor details and source reference in [this reply](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60792#discussion_r4228388505).

`parse_dec_only_prompt` supports both strings and token ID lists. Its list branch validates that the elements are integers and returns `TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=prompt)`.

`_build_prompt` unpacks the tuple before calling this helper, so `tokenize=True` remains supported. Forcing `tokenize=False` would unnecessarily restrict the existing input contract.

[The parser's string and list branches at the current PR head](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9a4453bf5e51db95dc46319db5a6080e6328ee22/vllm/renderers/inputs/preprocess.py).
Checked the image ordering and async rendering paths. Image data and UUIDs follow the rendered order, and the async wrapper uses the overridden `_apply_chat_template`.

self._apply_chat_template_async = make_async(
    self._apply_chat_template, executor=self._executor
)
```

This binds the overridden method on `DeepseekV41Renderer` as well, so both sync and async paths return `(prompt_raw, image_order)`. A separate async override should therefore not be necessary.

[Constructor and renderer implementation at the current PR head](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9a4453bf5e51db95dc46319db5a6080e6328ee22/vllm/renderers/deepseek_v4.py).

This is the same async-contract concern as the earlier comment; the existing constructor already wraps `self._apply_chat_template` with `make_async`, including the V4.1 override. The awaited result is therefore the same `(prompt_raw, image_order)` tuple consumed by `_build_prompt`.

I've added the constructor details and source reference in [this reply](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60792#discussion_r4228388505).

`parse_dec_only_prompt` supports both strings and token ID lists. Its list branch validates that the elements are integers and returns `TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=prompt)`.

`_build_prompt` unpacks the tuple before calling this helper, so `tokenize=True` remains supported. Forcing `tokenize=False` would unnecessarily restrict the existing input contract.

[The parser's string and list branches at the current PR head](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9a4453bf5e51db95dc46319db5a6080e6328ee22/vllm/renderers/inputs/preprocess.py).
